newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse to open new branch in Abuja.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse to open new branch in Abuja.

text.p: The Nigerian Stock Exchange is to open a new branch in the administrative capital Abuja, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"It is a long-term plan that started in 1993," Ndi Okereke-Onyuike, the deputy director-general told a news conference in the commercial capital Lagos, home to the headquarters of the Nigerian Stock Exchange.
She did say when it would open.
Last month, finance minister Anthony Ani said plans were afoot to break the monopoly of the Nigerian Stock Exchange by opening a second bourse in Abuja -- to be called the Stock Exchange of Nigeria.
The stock exchange has come under fire from the military government for what it describes as its failure to attract foreign investment and internationalise the market.
But the exchange in turn says government's delay in privatising big state-owned utilities discourages foreign investors.
Many traders in Lagos say another exchange is not necessary and have called on the government to support the existing one which has branches in Ibadan, Kaduna, Kano, Onitsha and Port Harcourt.
